posts.central_knowledge_unit: Pierre de Coubertin: Visionary and Founder of the Modern Olympics
posts.claim: Pierre de Coubertin is conventionally recognized as the founder or principal reviver of the modern international Olympic Games: he organized the 1894 Paris Congress, where delegates approved their re-establishment and created the IOC, leading to the Athens Games of 1896. He should not be described as the sole originator of Olympic revivalism, because earlier revival efforts and other contributors predated the 1894 initiative.

posts.central_knowledge_unit: Roberto Carlos' Brazil free kick in 1997: The physics behind 'impossible' strike - ESPN
posts.claim: Roberto Carlos’s free kick against France on 3 June 1997 was not physically impossible: a powerful, spinning ball over the unusually long roughly 35 m flight could follow a tightening, spiral-like curved trajectory as drag slows it, making its late bend appear abrupt. The published model supports that mechanism and says a comparable shot is possible under suitable speed, spin, and distance conditions; it does not establish an exact, fully reconstructed set of conditions for the individual kick.
posts.headline: Physics Shows Roberto Carlos’ 1997 Free‑Kick Was Not Impossible

posts.claim: The ballgame represents one of the most enduring and iconic features of ancient Mesoamerican civilization, yet its origins and evolution remain poorly understood, primarily associated with the Gulf Coast and southern Pacific coastal lowlands. While one early ballcourt dates to 1650 BCE from the Chiapas lowlands, ballcourts have remained undocumented in the Mesoamerican highlands until a millennium later, suggesting less involvement by highland civilizations in the ballgame’s evolution.
